questions.question: What color are temporary signs in construction and work zones?
questions.explanation: Temporary signs in work zones always have orange backgrounds with black writing or symbols.

questions.question: When you see a person crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until the person has completely crossed your path.
Honk your horn as you drive past them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person has completely crossed your path.
questions.explanation: You must stop for people using white canes or guide dogs. Always give them the right-of-way.

questions.question: If your gas pedal gets stuck, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If your gas pedal gets stuck, shift into neutral, apply the brakes, and pull off the road safely. Turn off the engine once you stop. If the pedal stays stuck, call for help and do not drive the car.

questions.question: What is the speed limit in a school zone during school hours?
questions.explanation: A five-sided sign marks a school zone. You must slow down to 15 mph during school hours and when children are present. Always drive carefully in areas with children.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must stop for other traffic.
Traffic is entering from another road. Move to another lane if you can so other drivers can merge safely.
Traffic is entering from another road. Stay in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is entering from another road. Move to another lane if you can so other drivers can merge safely.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic will be merging into your lane. Check your side and rear mirrors, then move to another lane if possible to give merging drivers space.

questions.question: What happens to collision risk each time you pass another car?
questions.explanation: Every time you pass another car, the risk of collision goes up. Only pass when you are certain it is safe.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to take your exit.
Make a U-turn to go back to your exit.
Put your car in reverse to go back.

questions.explanation: Do not make sudden moves to catch your exit. Always continue to the next exit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks are allowed on the narrow bridge ahead.
The bridge ahead only allows one direction of traffic.
Only one car can cross the bridge at a time.
The bridge ahead is too narrow to pass or meet a truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bridge ahead is too narrow to pass or meet a truck.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that the bridge ahead may be too narrow to meet or pass a truck. Drive carefully.

questions.question: You are on a multilane highway and see or hear an emergency vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
Slow down, move to give the emergency vehicle space, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to give the emergency vehicle space, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights, slow down, create a clear path, and stop. Do not try to outrun the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells you a steep hill is coming. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: What is a driving distraction?

options.text: Anything that makes you swerve while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A driving distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving. Distractions can happen at any time and place. They can cause crashes, property damage, injuries, and death.

questions.question: What should you do before turning?
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal three to four seconds before you turn. This helps other drivers know what you plan to do.

questions.question: Which of these commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Not paying attention to the road
Driving too fast for the conditions

questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of crashes. Not paying attention can cause you to hit other vehicles. Most rear-end crashes happen when drivers follow too closely behind other vehicles.

questions.question: When an officer directs traffic at a working traffic light, what should drivers do?

options.text: Watch what other cars are doing.

questions.explanation: Traffic lights control traffic flow and prevent crashes. Everyone must obey the signals, but when an officer is directing traffic, follow the officer's directions instead of the light.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing?
questions.explanation: When you see a railroad crossing sign, slow down, look for a train, and be ready to stop. If red lights are flashing or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Do not go around the gate.

questions.question: Roads are most dangerous at the start of light rain because oil and water mix to make a slippery film.
questions.explanation: Wet roads can be as slippery as icy roads, so slow down in rain. You need more distance to stop and may skid on turns. Roads are most dangerous at the start of rain because the water mixes with road oils that have not washed away yet.

questions.question: What should you do when driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog?

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down, let them cross, and be ready to stop. This keeps them safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming up ahead.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Take turns more slowly than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take turns more slowly than normal.
questions.explanation: Speeding on slippery roads is dangerous, especially on turns and curves. Approach turns much slower in slippery conditions than you normally would.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow traffic light?

options.text: Speed up to avoid a red light.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Watch what other cars are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light is coming. Stop unless you are already crossing the intersection.

questions.question: Before you start the car, you should:

options.text: Make sure only back seat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure everyone in the car has buckled their seat belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure everyone in the car has buckled their seat belt.
questions.explanation: Make a habit of buckling your seat belt every time you get in the car. Make sure all passengers do the same before you start the engine.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A crossroad is ahead. Be ready for other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: A crossroad is ahead. Be ready for other traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is coming up ahead.

questions.question: Driving too fast:

options.text: Saves time and gets you to your destination quicker.
Makes serious injury and death more likely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes serious injury and death more likely.
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of car crashes. It does not save time and leads to poor driving decisions.

questions.question: You should check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder when:

options.text: Pulling away from or toward a curb.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you move your car. This includes turning, changing lanes, and pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: Which statement is true about seat belts and child restraints?

options.text: Never place a baby or small child in the front seat of a car with airbags.
Airbags can hurt a baby or small child, even in a minor crash.
All passengers must use a seat belt or child restraint.

questions.explanation: Always buckle your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce the chance of injury or death in a crash. Children 12 and under should sit in the back seat properly restrained. Never place a rear-facing car seat in the front seat if there is a front airbag.

questions.question: Which substances can affect your ability to drive?

options.text: Cough syrup and cold medicine with codeine or antihistamines.

questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair your driving, including tranquilizers, sedatives, marijuana, and over-the-counter cough syrups and cold or allergy medicines that contain alcohol, codeine, or antihistamines.

questions.question: When you see a school bus stopped with flashing lights and its signal arm extended, you must:

options.text: Drive slowly at 15 mph if no children are visible.
Drive at normal speed but watch for children.

questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when a school bus has flashing lights and its signal arm extended. Stay stopped until the arm is pulled back and the bus starts moving. This rule applies whether you are going the same direction or coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: You must always follow the directions of a school crossing guard.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and follow instructions from crossing guards, signs, and police officers. Drive carefully in school zones.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: An orange and red triangle on the back of a vehicle means it is slow-moving. This includes farm tractors, road maintenance vehicles, and carts pulled by animals.

questions.question: The most common driving mistake when backing up is not looking both ways behind the car.
questions.explanation: Many drivers make mistakes when backing up because they do not look both ways behind them. Mirrors do not show everything. Turn your body and head to look through the rear window to see as much as possible.
